text: Given its role in spinal flexion, variations of the crunch are viable options for dynamically working the rectus abdominis. Although somewhat speculative, there is a sound rationale for performing traditional crunch variations to target the upper abdominal region and performing reverse crunch variations to develop the lower aspect of the muscle. This hypothesis is consistent with the anatomical design of the rectus abdominis. Not only do the tendinous intersections suggest some degree of functional independence of the muscle, but its upper and lower aspects are segmentally innervated by the ventral rami of the lower six or seven thoracic nerves (56), providing a further mechanism for selective activation.
